exposure: Induction of labour (IOL) at 41 weeks gestation
Spontaneous onset of labour (SOL) at 41 weeks gestation
Spontaneous onset of labour (SOL) at 42 weeks gestation
cohort: Pregnant women who delivered in Sweden between 2016 and 2021, with pregnancies beyond 41 weeks of gestation.
finding: Inducing labour at gestational week 41 was associated with significantly higher risks of adverse maternal and foetal outcomes, including caesarean deliveries, vacuum extraction, blood loss >1000 ml, stillbirths, and low Apgar scores, compared to spontaneous labour onset at the same gestational age.
mod_finding: The IOL group at gestational week 41 had higher rates of caesarean deliveries and vacuum extraction compared to SOL at 41 weeks, and higher rates of caesarean deliveries but lower rates of vacuum extraction compared to SOL at 42 weeks.
